title: Tiered approval thresholds
description: Actions are scored for risk, and each risk tier maps to an approval requirement: low-risk actions are auto-approved, medium-risk need one approver, high-risk need two. Thresholds are set in policy, not in code, so they can be tuned without redeploying. Every decision records the tier and the rule that fired. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers scoring actions into risk tiers.

title: Dual-control (four-eyes) approval
description: Consequential actions require two independent approvers: the second approver must be a different person who reviews the same context packet. This four-eyes principle catches mistakes and blocks unilateral abuse. The gateway enforces approver independence cryptographically where identities are managed. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers requiring two distinct approver identities.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: ["amy", "amy"], 2: ["amy", "bob"], 3: ["amy", "bob", "amy"]}
approvals = CFG[LEVEL]
requester = "amy"
distinct = [a for a in approvals if a != requester]
ok = len(set(distinct)) >= 2
print("approvals:", approvals, "| requester:", requester, "| dual-control satisfied:", ok)

title: Time-boxed approval request
description: Every approval request carries a time-to-live. If no human responds before the TTL, the request expires and the default is deny: the action does not proceed on silence. Time-boxing prevents stale approvals from authorizing actions long after the context changed. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers expiring unanswered requests at TTL.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Approval with context packet
description: The approver never decides blind: each request bundles a context packet with who is acting, what will happen, why it is needed, and how to reverse it. The packet is immutable once submitted, so the approver's decision is tied to exact facts. Packets are archived with the decision for audit. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers bundling who/what/why/reversible-steps.

title: Delegated approval chains
description: An approver can delegate authority within policy bounds: the delegation names the delegate, the scope, and the expiry. The gateway validates the whole chain from the original authority to the final approver. Delegations outside policy bounds are rejected before they can be used. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers validating delegation chains to the original authority.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: ["ceo", "vp"], 2: ["ceo", "vp", "mgr"], 3: ["ceo", "vp", "mgr", "lead"]}
chain = CFG[LEVEL]
authority = {"ceo": 3, "vp": 2, "mgr": 1, "lead": 1}  # max delegation depth
depth_ok = all(authority.get(p, 0) >= len(chain) - 1 - i for i, p in enumerate(chain))
print("chain:", " -> ".join(chain), "| valid:", depth_ok)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
